svg.text: TRANSFER PUMP P-101 — VSD POWER AND CONTROL
90 kW variable speed · duty/assist with P-102 · P-102 is identical, drawn on SCH-0111
The drive's thermal model only infers it.
Start command (SCADA in Remote, pushbutton in Local); wet well level LIT-101; discharge flow FIT-101; valve position ZSO-101; seal flow; low-low
float; thermistor relay; drive healthy; E-stop healthy; feeder available; selector position.
If ALL permissives true AND start command present AND (this pump is duty OR assist is called) THEN energise run command. Speed from PID on discharge
flow against SCADA setpoint, clamped between min and max. Duty rotation on run hours.
PLC DO → KA101 → hardwired run command to VSD-101 term 18. PLC AO 4–20 mA → speed reference. Hardwired dry-run trip →
drive external fault. Safety relay → STO.
Drive running and drive healthy hardwired; speed, current, power, fault codes and run hours over EtherNet/IP; running lamp at MCC and LCS; FIT-101
confirms the pump is actually moving water.
Drive trip → healthy DI drops, run command removed, standby called after delay. Motor over-temperature → KT101 opens, latched alarm.
Dry-run → hardwired float trips the drive DIRECTLY, independent of the PLC. Broken 4–20 mA → drive detects live-zero loss and holds
last speed with an alarm. Network failure → hardwired run/stop and speed reference still work.
1. LOCAL MODE ENFORCES EVERY PERMISSIVE AND EVERY TRIP. Local changes who gives the command, not what protects the machine. A Local mode that
drops the dry-run and thermistor trips is how a 90 kW pump is destroyed by someone who reasonably assumed it was protected.
2. The low-low float (path 05) is HARDWIRED into the drive's external fault input as well as being read by the PLC. Asset protection worth tens of thousands
of dollars must not depend solely on software that can be forced during commissioning. Verified at FAT with the PLC in program-stop (test I-67).
3. Critical inputs (drive healthy, thermistor, stop, seal water) are wired NORMALLY CLOSED so a broken wire reads as a fault, not as healthy.
4. Both selector positions are read as separate digital inputs so the PLC can distinguish Local, Remote and Off — and detect a selector fault if both read true.
5. The speed reference is hardwired 4–20 mA with monitoring over EtherNet/IP. A network fault must not leave a duty pump at an unknown speed. Trade-off:
all-comms is cheaper and gives richer diagnostics. This is a client standards question, not an absolute — see design basis 1.8.
6. Feeder breaker Q11 is selected from the DRIVE MANUAL, not from motor FLC. It protects the cable and the drive input, not the motor.
RAW WATER TRANSFER PUMP STATION — MCC-01
